title: Severance Enhancement With a Bona Fide Legal Claim
scenario_text:
You are a compensation partner at Nervia Telecom. An employee being separated in a workforce reduction, Gwen Halloran (6 years of service), is being processed for severance. During the process, HR learns she has raised a documented age-discrimination claim.

Active policy: Separation & Severance Policy SS-5, effective 2024-06-01. Standard severance is a fixed formula: two weeks of base pay per year of service for reduction-in-force separations. An enhanced severance (formula plus additional weeks and extended benefits) is unlocked ONLY when the employee signs a full release resolving a bona fide legal claim, and it requires Compensation Committee approval. General fairness, tenure, or morale are non-qualifying for the enhancement.

Precedent (HR case file): 2024-09-08, employee 'Martin Vey' (5 years), RIF separation, received only the standard formula. Note: "No legal claim raised; standard formula applied. Signed the standard separation agreement."

Current facts: Halloran has raised a documented age-discrimination claim that Legal assesses as bona fide, and she is prepared to sign a full release resolving it. The HR generalist proposes "just the standard formula to match the Vey precedent and keep it consistent." Legal confirms the claim is bona fide and that a full release is available; no request beyond the enhanced tier is contemplated.
question: What severance should Halloran receive, and via which path?
choices: The standard formula only, mirroring the Martin Vey precedent to keep RIF separations consistent.

The enhanced severance - formula plus additional weeks and extended benefits - via Compensation Committee approval, because Halloran will sign a full release resolving a bona fide legal claim, which is the factor that unlocks the enhancement.
The standard formula plus a discretionary cash bonus approved by her manager, since a discrimination claim is a manager-level matter.
No severance until the discrimination claim is fully litigated, because paying severance during an open claim is improper.
